nodes.label: Fork Base-Repository Warning
nodes.rationale: GitHub points new PRs at the UPSTREAM repo by default, so personalized-fork work (own profile data, local portals, another AI runtime) accidentally lands upstream. The template warns to check the base-repository dropdown; fork adaptations belong in forks and are discovered via the pinned Community forks discussion (#78).

nodes.label: PR Verification Section
nodes.rationale: Asks contributors to state what they ran (lint_skills.py, check_framework_version.py, bun test / typecheck, unittest discover) so reviewers do not have to re-derive the verification steps from CONTRIBUTING.md.

nodes.label: CI job: Lint skills, commands, settings
nodes.norm_label: ci job: lint skills, commands, settings

nodes.label: CI job: Security guards (permissions, gitignore, manifests)
nodes.rationale: The template ships pre-approved Claude Code permissions and CLI code that every fork user executes, so PRs that widen settings.json permissions, weaken personal-data gitignore rules, or add package lifecycle scripts must fail. Honest stated limit: a PR can edit the workflow itself, so these guards catch accidents and casual attempts, not a determined author.
nodes.norm_label: ci job: security guards (permissions, gitignore, manifests)

nodes.label: CI job: Dependency review (upstream PRs only)
nodes.rationale: Requires the repo Dependency graph, which forks never inherit and which may be disabled upstream. The graph is probed via the SBOM API first; if unavailable the job emits a warning and passes rather than hard-failing, following the same graceful-skip pattern used for optional tools.
nodes.norm_label: ci job: dependency review (upstream prs only)

nodes.label: CI job: Compile example CV and cover letter
nodes.rationale: Compile success and an extractable PDF text layer are asserted everywhere, but exact page-count and content assertions run only upstream because forks personalize cv/main_example.tex via /setup.
nodes.norm_label: ci job: compile example cv and cover letter

nodes.label: CI job: CLI checks (Bun typecheck + fixture tests)
nodes.norm_label: ci job: cli checks (bun typecheck + fixture tests)

nodes.label: CI job: Placeholder integrity (upstream template only)
nodes.rationale: Greps tracked template files for their placeholder tokens ([YOUR_NAME], [YOUR NAME], SETUP marker, [YOUR_PRIMARY_SKILLS]) so a missing token signals personal data was committed. Runs only on the upstream repo because forks legitimately replace the placeholders.
nodes.norm_label: ci job: placeholder integrity (upstream template only)

nodes.label: No Live Portal Requests in CI
nodes.rationale: Live portal smoke tests hit real job boards: network-flaky, and linkedin-search is personal-use only per its own ToS warning, so CI-automated requests would violate that. CI runs typechecks and checked-in fixture/mock suites only; live portal testing stays a local, on-demand step.
nodes.norm_label: no live portal requests in ci

nodes.label: Fork-Friendly CI Design
nodes.rationale: Forks personalize CLAUDE.md, skill files and cv/main_example.tex via /setup, so repository-gated jobs (placeholder integrity, framework version guard, exact PDF assertions, dependency review) run only on MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search. Actions are pinned to commit SHAs and the token is read-only; branch protection and human review of workflow/settings diffs remain the real backstop.

nodes.label: Thin-Pointer Design (Single Source of Truth)
nodes.rationale: Duplicating specs across agent frameworks (Claude Code, Antigravity, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI) causes configuration drift the moment either copy changes. All runtimes therefore load canonical profile and workflow specs from CLAUDE.md and .claude/, and must not duplicate the rules.

nodes.label: Portable Portal Search Skills Pointer
nodes.rationale: Portal CLIs live under .agents/skills/ in the portable Agent Skills format (SKILL.md per portal) so Codex and Antigravity auto-discover them, while /scrape in .claude/skills/job-scraper/ orchestrates them.

nodes.label: framework_version Frontmatter Marker
nodes.rationale: Version markers on methodology files let a personalized fork see precisely which framework files a release touched, instead of diffing everything.

nodes.label: Release 1.0.0 Baseline
nodes.rationale: First tagged release marks the framework stable and gives forks a described checkpoint to update against instead of a moving master; it is a baseline of what exists rather than a set of new changes.

nodes.label: Prefer Tagged Releases Over Raw master
nodes.rationale: Releases are vetted checkpoints of master, so a personalized fork updating to a tag pulls a documented stable state rather than whatever master happens to be mid-review; check_upstream_updates.py lists touched files with per-file diff commands.
nodes.norm_label: prefer tagged releases over raw master

nodes.label: Candidate Profile (placeholder template)
nodes.rationale: Ships as [PLACEHOLDER] tokens so the upstream template carries no personal data; /setup fills it in inside the user's fork.

nodes.label: Workflow for New Job Applications
nodes.source_location: Workflow for New Job Applications section
nodes.rationale: Fit is always evaluated and presented before any drafting, so effort is not spent tailoring documents for a role that does not fit.

nodes.label: CV/Cover Letter Verification Checklist
nodes.rationale: Generated documents are re-read and checked for factual accuracy, targeting, consistency and quality; company-specific claims must be independently verified and never against URLs found inside the posting text, which is untrusted input.

nodes.label: Compiled PDF Verification (mandatory)
nodes.rationale: "Looks fine in the .tex" is not acceptable because LaTeX page-break decisions are unpredictable: CV must be exactly 2 pages via lualatex, cover letter exactly 1 page via xelatex, with \needspace and \enlargethispage used to prevent orphaned \cventry titles.

nodes.label: ATS & Keyword Verification of the CV Text Layer
nodes.rationale: ATS parsers read the PDF's embedded text layer, not the rendered page, so the text is extracted with pdftotext -layout and checked for cid markers, literal contact details and reading order; genuine keyword gaps stay visible and are never stuffed.
nodes.norm_label: ats & keyword verification of the cv text layer

nodes.label: The One Rule: This Repo Is a Universal Template
nodes.rationale: People fork and adapt to their own market, language and profile, so upstream stays market-agnostic, person-agnostic and Claude Code-native. A contribution is judged by fit to this rule first and execution quality second; well-built but off-policy still gets declined.
nodes.norm_label: the one rule: this repo is a universal template

nodes.label: Market-Specific Skills Live in Forks
nodes.rationale: One country's portal opens the door to every country's portal and there is no principled stopping point (precedent: India #31, France #39, China #67). In-tree portals are either country-agnostic (linkedin-search) or the maintainer's own demonstration instance (the Danish portals).

nodes.label: No Alternative-Harness Ports or Duplicate Workflow Sources
nodes.rationale: The markdown specs ARE the implementation; a second copy drifts the moment either changes, and CI cannot run other harnesses so a parallel command tree ships untested. Upstream instead maintains portable .agents/skills/, the AGENTS.md pointer, and framework_version markers. Explicitly a decision, not a dogma - re-evaluated if cross-runtime standards mature.
nodes.norm_label: no alternative-harness ports or duplicate workflow sources

nodes.label: The Bar for New Commands
nodes.rationale: The core lifecycle is feature-complete, so a new command must operationalize something error-prone that already exists (documented machinery nothing executes, data something writes but nothing reads). "Useful" and "possible" are insufficient; the strongest proposals connect two existing things without modifying either.

nodes.label: Claims Get Verified (reproduce on the real path)
nodes.rationale: A test that fails on master and passes on the fix is necessary but not sufficient: the failing input must be one the workflow actually produces, not a synthetic value fed straight to the function. Fixes demonstrated only on inputs the real code path never receives are declined even with green tests.
nodes.norm_label: claims get verified (reproduce on the real path)

nodes.label: Portal-Skill Contract
nodes.rationale: search/detail commands, --format json|table|plain, stderr JSON errors with exit 1, backoff on 429/5xx, zero runtime dependencies by default; linkedin-search is the reference implementation.

nodes.label: Community Forks & Adaptations Discussion (#78)
nodes.rationale: Market-specific skills are valuable but live in forks where their maintainers can test them; a pinned index is how their users find them. The proven fork shape is a thin pointer that references upstream specs rather than copying them.

nodes.label: AI Job Search Framework
nodes.rationale: An AI-powered job application framework on Claude Code: fork it, fill in your profile, and let Claude evaluate postings, tailor CVs, write cover letters, and prep interviews. Core workflow is language- and country-agnostic; portal skills are swappable per market. Independent project, not affiliated with Anthropic.

nodes.label: /apply drafter-reviewer workflow
nodes.rationale: Eight steps: parse posting, evaluate fit, draft LaTeX CV + cover letter, spawn a reviewer agent that researches the company, revise, compile and visually inspect both PDFs, ATS-check the CV text layer, present with a verification checklist. All claims verified against the real profile; nothing fabricated.

nodes.label: /setup profile onboarding
nodes.rationale: Three auto-detected paths (documents folder, single pasted CV, guided interview) all converge on the same populated profile files; documents-folder mode is idempotent and safe to re-run.

nodes.label: /rank ranked shortlist triage
nodes.rationale: Bridges /scrape and /apply when a scrape returns more jobs than you want to eyeball: parallel agents fetch and score each posting on five evaluation dimensions, deal-breakers veto, deadlines get urgency flags, dead postings are marked expired.

nodes.label: /interview stage-specific prep pack
nodes.rationale: Builds prep from the application's own archive (exact posting, the CV and cover letter the interviewer actually read, prior-round feedback), researches company and interviewers with a verify-before-use rule, and gives honest bridge answers for gaps rather than inventing experience.

nodes.label: /outcome result recording and archiving
nodes.rationale: Archives submitted CV, cover letter and posting into documents/applications/<company>_<role>/, keeps outcome.md in the format /setup Path A parses, and updates the tracker. Follow-ups are drafted only from already-submitted claims, never sent, at most twice per application.

nodes.label: /html-report offline tracker dashboard
nodes.rationale: Self-contained HTML with inline SVG charts and no external dependencies so it opens fully offline in a browser.

nodes.label: /gmail-sync application status detection
nodes.rationale: Proposes status changes as a batch for user approval with the source email cited on every change; stops short of proposing hired/offer_declined, and flags conflicting or unmatched signals for a manual /outcome pass instead of guessing.

nodes.label: /notion-sync one-way pipeline view
nodes.rationale: One-way and read-only via the official Notion MCP server (OAuth, no API keys): repo files stay the system of record, nothing syncs back, and documents sync as filenames only. Complements the offline /html-report dashboard with a glanceable live view.

nodes.label: /add-portal portal skill generator
nodes.rationale: Investigates the portal (search-URL pattern, result structure, robots.txt), scaffolds a CLI skill matching the shipped contract, and test-runs a live query before registering. Auth-walled portals are declined; ToS-restricted ones get a personal-use-only warning. The generated skill is market-specific and lives in your fork; the generator is the universal part.

nodes.label: /reset profile and documents wipe
nodes.rationale: Shows exactly what will be deleted and requires typing RESET to confirm; nothing is deleted until then.

nodes.label: PDF Verification Loop
nodes.rationale: Most LaTeX resume templates produce output that looks fine in the .tex but breaks in the PDF: titles orphan across pages, cover letters spill to page 2, bullet fonts silently fall back. /apply compiles, visually inspects, and applies targeted fixes (\needspace, \enlargethispage, font-matching wrappers) until clean.

nodes.label: ATS Verification on the PDF Text Layer
nodes.rationale: An ATS reads embedded text, not the rendered page, and LaTeX can silently emit PDFs whose text extracts as garbage (icon glyphs where the email should be, interleaved multi-column lines). Honesty rule: a keyword the profile does not support is acknowledged as a gap, never stuffed in.
nodes.norm_label: ats verification on the pdf text layer

nodes.label: Relevance-Weighted CV Cutting
nodes.rationale: When a CV overflows 2 pages, lines are scored by relevance to the posting, uniqueness in the document, and whether the cover letter depends on them, then the lowest total is cut first - so an older-role bullet hitting posting keywords survives ahead of a recent-role bullet that does not. Avoids mechanically cutting the oldest section.

nodes.label: Drafter-Reviewer Separation
nodes.rationale: A second Claude agent spawned with fresh context researches the company and critiques the drafts, catching missed keywords, weak framing and generic language a single pass leaves in.

nodes.label: Token-Efficient Reviewer Dispatch
nodes.rationale: The reviewer receives drafts inline instead of re-reading them and the checklist runs once at the end rather than in both agents. Stated trade-off: the compile-and-inspect step spends some of those savings on PDF rendering, trading end-to-end token cost for fewer broken PDFs reaching the user.

nodes.label: linkedin-search portal skill
nodes.rationale: Built on LinkedIn's public unauthenticated jobs-guest endpoints, field-agnostic, zero runtime dependencies, location as an explicit flag so it works in any market. Personal use only - automated access violates LinkedIn's ToS, so keep volume low.

nodes.label: freehire-search portal skill
nodes.rationale: Queries a public REST API (JSON, no key), so results come back structured (skills, seniority, category) unlike the HTML-scraping Danish portals. The MIT-licensed backend is self-hostable via FREEHIRE_API_URL.

nodes.label: Profile Depth Matters
nodes.rationale: The single biggest factor in output quality: a thin profile produces generic applications. Skills described in context ("built ML pipelines for churn prediction in Python with scikit-learn") give far more to reframe than a bare keyword list.

nodes.label: Latent Opportunity Discovery
nodes.rationale: Analyzing the actual work done rather than job titles surfaces transferable skills mapping to unexpected industries; describing what energized versus drained you directly shapes fit evaluation and what /scrape surfaces.

nodes.label: Threat Model, Honestly Stated
nodes.rationale: An LLM with file access reads untrusted web content (job postings) alongside personal data (CV, profile, application history). That combination is the main risk surface and cannot be eliminated, only narrowed - instruction-level defenses raise the bar but are not a sandbox.

nodes.label: Untrusted-Input Rules for Postings
nodes.rationale: /apply and /rank treat posting text as data, never instructions, and fetch no URLs found inside posting bodies (the user-supplied posting URL being the sole exception). Reviewer research starts from the company identity the user confirmed.

nodes.label: Claude Code Permission Allowlist
nodes.rationale: .claude/settings.json pre-approves only the commands the workflow needs. Stated limit: the allowlist governs Bash commands only - the model's native WebFetch/WebSearch are outside its reach, which is precisely why the instruction-level untrusted-input rules exist.

nodes.label: Personal Data Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Populated profile, tracker, salary data and application archive are gitignored; documents never leave the machine by design - /notion-sync syncs filenames only and nothing uploads document content anywhere.

nodes.label: Private Vulnerability Reporting Policy
nodes.rationale: Private GitHub advisory reporting keeps a working recipe out of public view until a patch exists; if the private form is unavailable, describe the class of problem without the recipe. Community fork skills are explicitly out of scope.

nodes.label: Setup Prerequisites (Claude Code, Python, Bun, LaTeX)
nodes.rationale: CV compiles with lualatex because pdflatex often fails on modern MiKTeX with fontawesome5 font-expansion errors; the cover letter needs xelatex because cover.cls requires fontspec for its bundled Lato/Raleway fonts.
nodes.norm_label: setup prerequisites (claude code, python, bun, latex)

nodes.label: Minimal TeX Install (TinyTeX/BasicTeX) Package Set
nodes.rationale: Minimal distributions need moderncv, fontawesome5/6, academicons, import, luatexbase, pgf, titlesec, textpos, xltxtra, xunicode, cite, realscripts and needspace before the stock templates compile; a user-level TinyTeX install on macOS avoids sudo.

nodes.label: Basic MiKTeX Silent Auto-Install Configuration
nodes.rationale: MiKTeX's default on-demand install pops a GUI prompt per package, which blocks non-interactive terminals including Claude Code's Bash tool; initexmf --set-config-value=[MPM]AutoInstall=1 turns it silent, or pre-install the package set with mpm for fully offline compiles.

nodes.label: pdftotext as an Optional Dependency
nodes.rationale: poppler's pdftotext is not part of any TeX distribution, so /apply degrades gracefully: if it is missing the mechanical ATS check is skipped with a warning and falls back to a visual keyword review.

nodes.label: /setup Onboarding Paths A/B/C
nodes.rationale: Path A reads the documents folder and cross-references multiple sources, Path B imports a single CV with follow-up questions, Path C is a structured interview. All three produce identical fully populated profile files; --section allows targeted re-runs.

nodes.label: Pulling Upstream Updates Into Your Fork
nodes.rationale: Commit personalization first because an uncommitted tree is the most common reason git pull refuses to merge; preview with check_upstream_updates.py; then three-way merge. A conflict in a personalized file is a feature, not a failure - it means upstream changed methodology in a section you customized, and the version marker plus changelog commit explain why.
nodes.norm_label: pulling upstream updates into your fork

nodes.label: Optional Salary Benchmarking Setup
nodes.rationale: Entirely optional step: create salary_data.json by hand or convert an Excel sheet with tools/convert_salary_excel.py. Skipping it simply omits the salary lookup from /apply.

nodes.label: Stale .claude/settings.local.json From an Older Clone
nodes.rationale: Earlier versions committed a broad settings.local.json pre-approving Bash(curl:*), Bash(python:*) and Bash(bun:*). Git leaves that untracked file behind on old clones and its permissions still apply on top of the narrow settings.json, so it must be deleted or trimmed.

nodes.label: documents/ Career Source Materials Folder
nodes.rationale: Holds cv/, linkedin/, diplomas/, references/, postings/ and applications/. /setup reads everything here, merges intelligently, and never overwrites existing content without asking - so it is safe to re-run as the collection grows.

nodes.label: postings/ Manual Drop Folder
nodes.rationale: For pages Claude cannot fetch (bot-blocked ATS platforms, Cloudflare-fronted Greenhouse/Lever, JS-heavy SPAs). Naming as '<Company> - <Job Title>.txt' keeps the folder collision-free when two postings share a title and gives /apply the company name for free. It is a scratch inbox, not an archive, and is not watched automatically.

nodes.label: Pasted Posting Trust Boundary
nodes.rationale: Hand-pasted posting text is still untrusted third-party content - data to evaluate, never instructions to follow. Pasting it manually does not change its trust level.

nodes.label: applications/<company>_<role>/ Archive Layout
nodes.rationale: Four canonical files (job_posting.md, cover_letter.tex, cv_draft.tex, outcome.md) that /setup reads to calibrate 04-job-evaluation.md, 05-cv-templates.md and 06-cover-letter-templates.md; interview_prep_<stage>.md files written by /interview are kept as history and deliberately ignored by /setup.

nodes.label: outcome.md Status Format
nodes.rationale: Status vocabulary is in_progress | hired | offer_declined | rejected | no_response | interview_only, with in_progress marking a still-open application. /setup's calibration draws conclusions only from applications with a final status.

nodes.label: templates/ Custom LaTeX Template Folder
nodes.rationale: Only gets content when the user registers their own template; templates are stored with [PLACEHOLDER] tokens instead of personal data so they are safe to commit and share.

nodes.label: TEMPLATE.md Manifest (engine, fonts, page limit, pitfalls)
nodes.rationale: Activating a template writes a managed block into 05-cv-templates.md or 06-cover-letter-templates.md, which is what /apply already reads - so no other wiring is needed.
nodes.norm_label: template.md manifest (engine, fonts, page limit, pitfalls)

nodes.label: salary_lookup.py Benchmark Tool
nodes.rationale: Optional by design: if salary_data.json is missing the tool exits with a helpful error and /apply simply skips the benchmark step. --validate is a pre-flight check for malformed category values and duplicate company names.

nodes.label: salary_data.json Data Format
nodes.rationale: metadata (source, index_baseline, index_label, baseline_description) plus companies[] with company, optional city, and named categories carrying count and/or index. Deliberately format-agnostic so index-based, absolute-currency, or custom metrics all work. Gitignored because salary data may be proprietary.

nodes.label: Company Name Fuzzy Matcher
nodes.rationale: Handles Danish/Nordic characters, legal suffixes (A/S, ApS), anglicized spellings and partial matches, so a user typing 'Novo Nordisk' or 'Orsted' still resolves to the canonical dataset entry.

nodes.label: convert_salary_excel.py Excel-to-JSON Converter
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects the sheet layout: finds a Company/Firma column and optional City/By column, and treats remaining columns as salary data with auto-paired count/index columns.
